page.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: Physical Copy Code Flaw Explained
page.meta_description: Grand Theft Auto VI heads to Vice City in the state of Leonida. What we know about the game, plus the reported physical copy code flaw.
page.tagline: Rockstar's return to Vice City comes with a new question for boxed buyers: what's actually inside the case?
overview: Grand Theft Auto VI is an upcoming action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games. It is due to be the eighth main entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V, and the sixteenth entry overall. The story follows the criminal duo of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, set in the fictional US state of Leonida — a take on Florida that includes the Miami-inspired Vice City.

Players will freely roam Leonida's open world. Rockstar's teams researched Miami and its surrounding areas extensively for the game's world, which parodies 2020s American culture. The protagonists' dynamic is inspired by Bonnie and Clyde, and the non-player characters were written to make sure players experience different areas of Vice City. Preliminary work on the title began in 2014 after Grand Theft Auto V's release, with principal production starting after Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in 2018. Rockstar confirmed the game was in development in February 2022, and that September footage from unfinished versions leaked online.

The 'physical copy code flaw' in the search bar comes from a run of news reports about boxed editions. Headlines claim GTA 6 PS5 codes are potentially being stolen from physical copies using a flashlight trick, that the physical edition is missing more than just its disc, and that a collector's box was sold early amid map leaks. These are press reports rather than anything Rockstar has confirmed in the sources we have, so treat the details carefully — but if you plan to buy a boxed copy, it's worth understanding what people are saying before you hand over your money.

how_to_play: Free roam the open world of Leonida, the Florida-inspired state that contains the Miami-style Vice City.
Follow the story of the criminal duo Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose partnership draws on the Bonnie and Clyde dynamic.
Explore different areas of Vice City through the game's NPCs, who were written to bring players into each part of the city.
If you're buying a boxed copy, check what the package actually contains — reports describe physical editions shipping without a disc.
tips: Before buying a boxed copy, read the retailer's listing carefully to see whether a disc is included or whether the box only holds a download code.
Inspect the seal and packaging when your copy arrives; the reported 'flashlight trick' involves codes being obtained from physical copies, so a tampered box is worth flagging immediately.
Redeem any code as soon as you get it home rather than leaving it sitting in the case.
Buy from a reputable retailer you can return to if something looks off with the packaging.
Be sceptical of early 'collector's box' listings and leaked map images — headlines about boxes sold early are unconfirmed reports, not official Rockstar announcements.

faq.q: What is the GTA 6 physical copy code flaw?
faq.a: It refers to a series of news reports claiming that codes inside GTA 6 physical copies could potentially be stolen using a so-called flashlight trick. The reports are unconfirmed in the sources we have, and Rockstar has not been quoted on them here.

faq.q: Does the physical edition include a disc?
faq.a: One headline states that the physical edition is 'missing more than just its disc', implying the boxed release does not contain a disc and relies on a code instead. Treat this as reported rather than officially confirmed.

faq.q: Which platform do the reports mention?
faq.a: The headlines specifically reference PS5 codes being potentially stolen from physical copies. A full platform list for the game is not provided in these sources.

faq.q: When is Grand Theft Auto VI out?
faq.a: The available sources describe the game as upcoming and do not confirm a release date, so we haven't listed one.

faq.q: What do we know about the game itself?
faq.a: It's an action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, the eighth main entry in the series and sixteenth overall. It's set in the fictional state of Leonida, based on Florida, and follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, with Vice City as its Miami-inspired centrepiece.
Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal duo whose dynamic is inspired by Bonnie and Clyde.

faq.q: How long has the game been in development?
faq.a: Preliminary work began in 2014 after Grand Theft Auto V launched, with principal production starting after Red Dead Redemption 2's launch in 2018. Rockstar confirmed the project in February 2022, and unfinished footage leaked that September.
